subject.title: fix(cli): load plugins for openclaw sandbox so OpenShell backend reports live status (#59528)

question: Should sandbox CLI commands activate every enabled plugin before running, or should OpenClaw add a narrower sandbox-backend registration path for backend managers only?
rationale: The current PR fixes the reported OpenShell path but changes the failure boundary for all sandbox commands; choosing broad activation versus a new scoped plugin contract is a maintainer product/runtime decision.

options.title: Use backend-scoped activation
options.body: Add a narrow way to activate only sandbox backend owners needed for registry entries, preserving Docker/SSH status when unrelated plugins fail.

options.title: Accept broad sandbox activation
options.body: Land the current shape and intentionally accept that any enabled plugin load failure can block sandbox CLI status and recreate commands.

options.title: Pause the PR
options.body: Keep the linked issue open while maintainers decide the permanent sandbox plugin registration contract.

recommendation.title: Use backend-scoped activation
recommendation.body: Add a narrow way to activate only sandbox backend owners needed for registry entries, preserving Docker/SSH status when unrelated plugins fail.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points to OpenShell backend ownership and CLI routing metadata work by this owner candidate.
